rules.title: 🕹️ Rules (based on the original XBill 2.1):
rules.1.head: Whack the Bills
rules.1.body: : Click or tap to take them out. Hit several overlapping Bills at once for a bigger score (number defeated squared × 5 points).
rules.2.head: Get the OS back
rules.2.body: : A Bill replaces a PC's OS with Wingdows and runs off with the stolen OS on his head. Whack him and he drops it — drag it back to a PC of the same type. Bills that escape come back later.
rules.3.head: Stop the sparks
rules.3.body: : If only one of two cable-connected PCs is Wingdows, a spark runs along the cable to the other. Dragging the bucket from the top-left onto a spark only restarts it from the beginning. To stop it for good, drag a dropped OS back onto the PC that is running Wingdows (it stops once neither end is Wingdows). A PC that Wingdows took over through a spark does not drop its old OS, so use an OS dropped by another Bill.
rules.4: The game ends when 1 or fewer PCs are still running. After each level you get a bonus based on uptime.
rules.5.head: Clear level 10 to win!
rules.5.body: On higher levels, more Bills come at once, faster, and steal OSes faster. Clear every level and you can download a certificate (image) with your name on it.

story.p1: Yet again, the fate of the world rests in your hands! An evil computer hacker, known only by his handle 'Bill', has created the ultimate computer virus. A virus so powerful that it has the power to transmute an ordinary computer into a toaster oven. (oooh!) 'Bill' has cloned himself into a billion-jillion micro-Bills. Their sole purpose is to deliver the nefarious virus, which has been cleverly disguised as a popular operating system.
story.p2: As System Administrator/Exterminator, your job is to keep Bill from succeeding at his task.
sbt.note1: An SBT is a non-transferable commemorative NFT. It has no monetary value.
sbt.note2: If issued, your address, clear date and serial number will be public on the blockchain (Polygon). You can delete the SBT yourself later, but the record of its issuance stays on the chain.
sbt.note3: Issuance is done later at the operator's discretion and is not guaranteed.
sbt.note4: Enter the address of your own wallet that works on Polygon (exchange deposit addresses cannot be used).
sbt.consent: I agree to the notes above
sbt.done: Received. The operator will issue it at a later date.
sbt.invalid: Invalid address format (42 characters starting with 0x).
sbt.duplicate: This address has already been requested.
sbt.limit: Today's request limit has been reached. Please try again tomorrow.
sbt.error: Could not send. Check your connection and try again.
sbt.closed: Requests are not being accepted right now.
sbt.checksum: The address seems to contain a typo (its upper/lower case pattern does not match). Please copy it again from your wallet.
sbt.note5: When you apply, your address, name and score are sent to our server for the operator to review. The name and score are deleted after the request is issued or declined. To prevent abuse, a non-reversible fingerprint of your connection is kept for 2 days.
